name: code_grep
title: Search code and text files
description: Use instead of `rg`/`grep` to find exact text (a string, identifier or comment) in indexed code and text files (markdown, config, data; not PDFs). `pattern` is literal unless `regex` is true. Rows `<line>: <text>` (`<line>:<col>,<col>: ...`: matches sharing a line; `<line>- ...`: context) sit under `# <file>` and `## <symbol>` (`##`: none) headers, after `key: value` lines: `stale` (edited since indexing), `skipped_files` (unsearchable), `total` (with `next_cursor`: hits from `cursor` on). A `path` or `language` no indexed file has is an error. Example: {"pattern":"cache_root(","path":"src/"}

pattern.description: Text to find, not empty; a literal unless `regex` is true.

regex.description: Treat `pattern` as a Rust regex; `^` and `$` match at every line.

path.description: Literal substring of the repo-relative path, e.g. `src/mcp/`; not a glob.

context.description: Lines before and after each hit, 0-10.

changed.description: Only files changed since rev (empty: HEAD) or in A..B; +importers adds importers.

name: code_outline
title: Outline a file
description: Use to see what a file contains before, or instead of, reading it: every symbol with its kind, signature and 1-based `line`/`end_line`, plus the file's imports. Feed a span to `code_read`. Code files only. `stale` means the file changed since it was indexed and is outlined as it is now. Example: {"path":"src/store.rs"}

name: code_read
title: Read a symbol or line span
description: Use to read the source of one function or type, or an exact line span, instead of the whole file. Pass `symbol` (plus `line` when several share the name), or a `line`..`end_line` span. A body over 128 KiB is cut, at a line end if it can, and flagged `truncated`: read on from `end_line` + 1. `stale`: the file changed since indexing and was parsed as it is now. Example: {"path":"src/store.rs","symbol":"open"}

symbol.description: Symbol whose body to return (exact name).

kind.description: With `symbol`: its kind, when several share the name.

line.description: First line of a span, 1-based. With `symbol`: a line inside the definition meant.

end_line.description: Last line of a span, inclusive (default: `line`). Not with `symbol`.

name: code_refs
title: Find call sites, implementations and importers
description: Use for what calls, implements or imports X, or which definition a use binds to (`relation`). Callers are call sites, not type uses or `use` lines. `match` `exact`: the name or a path ending in it; `substring`: any name holding it. `hits` maps files to rows: `line`, `callee` if not `name`, `stale` if edited since. `path` pins the definition there. Row `resolution` (omitted if `resolution_default`, else name_only): same_file, imported, scope_resolved (local binding), elsewhere (binds another), name_only (unchecked: `resolution_note`), external (not indexed), path_match (HTTP call to route `name` like `GET /a/{id}`, or a pinned handler's routes and calls; literal URLs; `ambiguous`: routes tie; `definition` of a call: its route). `importers`+`path`, no `name`: its importers `by_depth`. `cycles`: import cycles (`path`: its own). Example: {"name":"open_store","path":"src/store.rs"}

name.description: Name called, implemented or defined; for `importers`, whole segments of the import path.

path.description:
`callers`: file defining `name`, pinning that definition. `definition`: file holding the
reference (required). `importers`/`cycles`: that file (no `name`).

line.description:
Needs `path`. `callers`: 1-based line inside the definition meant, when several share the
name. `definition`: line of the reference (required).

column.description: `definition` only: 1-based column (default: where `name` occurs on the line).

resolution.description: `callers` only: keep rows of these resolutions, comma-separated.

changed.description: `callers` only: files changed since rev (empty: HEAD) or in A..B; +importers adds importers.

name: code_search
title: Search code by meaning
description: Use when you know what the code does but not a name or string in it: searches code chunks by meaning and returns pointers (path, `line`/`end_line`, symbol), not bodies; copies of a file share one hit (`also_at`). `lanes_unavailable` names lanes that did not run. Read a hit with `code_read`. Example: {"query":"retry a failed upload with backoff"}

query.description: What the code does, in plain words.

name: code_symbols
title: Find a definition
description: Use for "where is X defined" when you know (part of) the name: finds functions, types, constants and other symbols by name across the repository; a row is `"<path>:<line>: <signature>"`. Ranked: the exact name first, then prefix, then substring, then (with `fuzzy`) fuzzy matches; `stale`: files edited since the scan (lines current). Definitions only: for any text use `code_grep`. Example: {"name":"parse_config","kind":"function"}

kind.description: function, method, struct, enum, class, interface, trait, type, const, module, macro, route.

fuzzy.description: Also match the name as a fuzzy subsequence, ranked last.

changed.description: Only files changed since rev (empty: HEAD) or in A..B; +importers adds importers.

name: docs_search
title: Search documents
description: Use to find where a topic is discussed in the repository's documents (markdown, PDFs, Office, HTML, email, notebooks) instead of opening them. Ranks passages by meaning and words, filters first, and cites each hit (path, pages, section, lines). Code: `code_grep`/`code_search`. Example: {"query":"how releases are versioned"}

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

kind.description: Format: pdf, office, html, markdown, email, notebook, text or other.

keywords.description: Whole keywords, comma-separated; any one matches.

entity.description: Keep chunks naming an entity of this category, e.g. `PERSON`.

name: find_files
title: Find files
description: Use instead of `find`/`fd`/`ls -R` to locate a file by a fuzzy fragment of its name or path, or to list files when `query` is omitted; `files` holds paths. Covers code, documents and every other file git tracks; a query with one typo still finds its file. A `path_prefix` or `language` no listed file has is an error. Example: {"query":"readme"}

query.description: Fuzzy fragment of a file name or path; omit to list.

path_prefix.description: Only paths starting with this, e.g. `src/mcp/`.

min_lines.description: Only code files of at least this many lines, largest first; `files` maps path to lines.

changed.description: Only files changed since rev (empty: HEAD) or in A..B; +importers adds importers.

name: git_blame
title: Blame
description: Use instead of `git blame` for "who last changed this": per-line authorship of a file, a 1-based `line`..`end_line` span, or one `symbol` (at `rev`). `hunks`: `"<line>[-<end>] <sha>[ <old path>]"` (the rest of the row, when moved); `commits`: each sha's author, time, summary. Example: {"path":"src/store.rs","symbol":"open"}

line.description:
First line of a span, 1-based, as numbered at `rev`. With `symbol`: a line inside the
definition meant.

end_line.description: Last line of a span, inclusive (default: `line`). Needs `line`; not with `symbol`.

symbol.description: Blame this symbol's lines, as they are at `rev`, instead of a span.

name: git_diff
title: Diff and status
description: Use instead of `git status`/`git diff`. No arguments returns the working-tree status (staged, modified, untracked; 200 paths per list); a file `path` alone diffs its working tree against HEAD, or `from`/`to`; `structural` lists the symbols added and removed, and counts the `common` ones, instead of text hunks. A diff over 200 hunks or 128 KiB is cut (`truncated`). Example: {"path":"src/store.rs","from":"HEAD~1","to":"HEAD"}

path.description:
File to diff, or a directory ending in `/` to narrow the status; omit every argument for
the whole working-tree status.

to.description: New revision (default: the working tree). Needs `path`; not with `structural`.

structural.description: Symbol-level diff of `from` against the indexed working tree, instead of text hunks.

name: git_log
title: Commit history
description: Use instead of `git log`/`git show` for "what changed recently", "what touched this file", "which commit mentions X" or "what changed this function". `{}` lists recent commits; `path`, `query`/`author`, `path`+`symbol` or `rev` narrow it. A row is `"<sha> <summary>"`, `[introduced]`/`[removed]` after a symbol's sha; recent and directory lists add `files`: sha to path to change. `rev` shows one commit whole, with author and time. A symbol's or directory's history pages by commit window: follow `next_cursor`, even from an empty page (`window`). Example: {"path":"src/store.rs","limit":5}

path.description:
Only commits touching this file, or a directory (trailing `/`; 200 commits a page). Not with
`query` or `author`.

query.description: Words the commit message must all contain. Combines with `author` only.

author.description:
Words the author name or email must all contain; rows then name the author. Combines with
`query` only.

symbol.description: Commits that changed this symbol's body; needs `path`, combines with nothing else but `line`.

line.description: With `symbol`: 1-based line inside the definition meant, when several share the name.

rev.description: Show this one commit in full; `max_tokens` bounds its file list. Combines with nothing.

name: index_rescan
title: Re-index
description: Use after editing files, or when the index is empty or stale: re-indexes the given `paths`, or with no arguments the whole workspace, skipping unchanged files. Writes only basemind's cache, never the repository. Example: {"paths":["src/store.rs"]}

paths.description:
Repo-relative files or directories to re-index (default: the whole workspace, skipping
unchanged files).

name: index_status
title: Index status
description: Use when a result is unexpectedly empty or says "not indexed": reports how many files are indexed per language, whether a scan is running or the index is degraded, the cache directory, and the repository's branch and HEAD. Example: {}

name: memory_save
title: Save a note
description: Use to remember a decision, convention or finding for later sessions and other agents working in this repository. Saving an existing `key` replaces it. Notes are plain text on local disk: never save secrets. Example: {"key":"decision/auth-tokens","value":"Tokens rotate every 24h.","tags":["auth"]}

visibility.description: Memory tier: `group` (default) is shared across agents; `individual` scopes the entry to the calling agent.

name: memory_search
title: Recall notes
description: Use to recall what was saved with `memory_save`: `query` searches notes by meaning (by words when no model loads), `key` reads one, `prefix` lists by key prefix, and no arguments lists everything. Lists show 200 characters of a value; `key` reads it whole. Example: {"query":"token rotation"}

query.description: Search notes by meaning. At most one of `query`, `key`, `prefix`; none lists every note.

key.description: Read one note by exact key.

prefix.description: List notes whose key starts with this.

tag.description: Only notes carrying this tag. Not with `key`.

visibility.description: Memory tier: `group` (default) is shared across agents; `individual` scopes the entry to the calling agent.

limit.description: Max notes (default 10 for `query`, 100 for a listing). Not with `key`.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` of the previous listing page. Not with `query` or `key`.
